title: Q: Why must the container shape, surface texture AND temperature range be identical in the cooling-rate experiment?

The cooling constant K depends on the exposed area and on the nature of the surface. Two cups of different size, paint or polish do not share K, even in the same room.

The rate dθ/dt also depends on the excess θ − θ0. If one liquid is timed from 90°C to 70°C and the other from 50°C to 40°C, the excesses are different and the times do not measure heat capacity alone.
Only when the containers match and the upper and lower temperatures match does K, and the excess history, cancel in the ratio. Then m1 c1 / t1 = m2 c2 / t2.

exercises.question: Liquid A is cooled from 80°C to 60°C and liquid B from 50°C to 40°C in cups of different area. Can m c / t be set equal? Explain in steps.
steps: The areas differ, so K is not the same.
The temperature intervals differ, so the excesses are not the same function of time.
Both reasons stop K and (θ − θ0) from cancelling.
Therefore m_A c_A / t_A = m_B c_B / t_B is not justified.
The experiment has to be repeated in one cup over one shared interval.
exercises.answer: No. The surface factor and the temperature limits both differ.

summary: A cooling comparison of specific heats needs the same surface factor and the same temperature interval. Otherwise the times mix the effect of the cup and the effect of the excess temperature into the value of c.
